Abstract and Conclusions (HTML full text): SHAP interpretive robustness of a hybrid LightGBM/XGBoost/RF model measured by coefficient of variation over 10-fold CV on tabular landslide factors
problem: Single landslide-susceptibility models give unstable SHAP interpretations.
method: Heterogeneous hybrid of LightGBM, XGBoost and random forest interpreted with SHAP; 10-fold cross-validation; coefficient of variation (CV) of SHAP importances; McNemar tests for accuracy.
data: 347 landslide and 347 non-landslide points in Xi'an with conditioning factors (slope, elevation, LS factor, etc.) from a national landslide inventory 1949-2011.
evaluation: CV of SHAP importance across folds (lower = more robust); accuracy, F1, AUC; McNemar's chi-squared test.
findings: Hybrid CV 0.175 vs 0.208 (LightGBM), 0.240 (XGBoost) and 0.207 (RF) with comparable accuracy (abstract).
limitations: Ours: single region and small sample; stability only across CV folds (retraining), not input perturbation.

evidence: Abstract and results (HTML full text): LIME stability and fidelity with Weibull, Gamma, Beta and Pareto perturbation distributions on tabular CIC-IDS-2018
problem: LIME's normal-distribution perturbations fit poorly to skewed, imbalanced network-traffic features, giving unstable explanations.
method: Modified LIME sampling with Weibull, Gamma, Beta and Pareto distributions for DT, RF, K-NN and XGBoost classifiers; fidelity (R2) and stability score S compared with default LIME.
evaluation: Local surrogate R2 (fidelity) and stability score S across repeated explanations.
findings: Pareto gave the highest fidelity and stability, e.g. K-NN R2 = 0.9971, S = 0.9907 and DT R2 = 0.9267, S = 0.9797 (results).
limitations: Ours: one dataset family; stability of the sampling only, no prediction-preserving input perturbation.
qa_notes: Q6 one dataset; Q7 brief; Q10 repeated LIME runs.

evidence: Abstract and Methods (HTML full text): SHAP ranking stability across five biased/shifted Bank Account Fraud variants vs permutation importance
problem: Stable SHAP explanations may not reflect performance-based feature reliance under distribution shift.
method: Logistic regression, linear SVC and random forest; cross-variant evaluation; SHAP stability via Spearman correlation and top-5/top-10 overlap with the Base-model ranking (fixed model and retrained models); permutation importance with repeated permutations; bootstrap.
data: Bank Account Fraud dataset suite: Base plus five biased variants (group-size, prevalence, separability, temporal shift).
evaluation: Spearman rank correlation, top-k overlap, rank gaps between SHAP and permutation importance; classification metrics under imbalance.
findings: SHAP rankings stayed relatively stable across variants, but permutation importance showed weaker and more variable reliance on several SHAP-ranked features, so stable explanations did not guarantee reliable feature reliance (abstract).
limitations: Ours: data available on request only for processed files; single dataset suite.
repro: Data available on request; no code link.

evidence: Abstract and SHAP audit Step 4 (HTML full text): perturbation stability of SHAP (10 Gaussian-noise copies per instance) on tabular US-Accidents and UK STATS19 (borderline: one of four audit steps)
problem: SHAP explanations in crash-severity models are rarely audited for faithfulness and stability.
method: Five classifiers with temporal splits; isotonic calibration; four-step quantitative SHAP audit (sanity, deletion/insertion faithfulness, perturbation stability via local-Lipschitz style test with 10 perturbed copies, sigma = 0.01 of feature SD plus one binary toggle); cross-jurisdiction transfer.
data: US-Accidents (7.0 million records, 2016-2023) and UK STATS19 (about 1,010,000 records, 2016-2022).
evaluation: Low-stability fraction of instances under perturbation; deletion faithfulness; ECE; transfer metrics.
findings: Explanation stability failed at realistic perturbation levels: 54.3% of instances were low-stability at sigma = 0.05, driven by spatial sparsity in geohash cells (abstract).
limitations: Authors: US label measures disruption duration, not injury (abstract). Ours: perturbations not filtered to preserve predictions.
repro: Code, split indices and artifacts: github.com/malhawarat/sae-xcrash.

evidence: Abstract and Secs.3-7 (HTML full text): SHAP global-ranking agreement across bootstrap refits optimised jointly with AUPRC on 5 tabular attrition benchmarks
problem: Attrition models are tuned for discrimination, yet nothing requires their SHAP driver ranking to survive retraining.
method: Bi-objective hyperparameter optimisation (cost-sensitive AUPRC and expected agreement of SHAP global rankings across bootstrap refits); U-statistic estimator; minimum-variance ensemble weights; multi- vs single-objective solvers.
data: Five public HR-attrition benchmarks (1.4-50.6% positives), incl. IBM-HR.
evaluation: Expected ranking agreement across refits; AUPRC; statistical tests between solvers.
findings: Attribution variance is not a proxy for explanation stability (minimising it picked the least stable learner on every benchmark); no test separated multi- from single-objective solvers at a practitioner's budget (abstract).
limitations: Authors: the stability objective must itself be estimated (abstract). Ours: retraining stability only.
qa_notes: Q8 data public, code not seen; Q9 HR data context; Q10 bootstrap refits.

evidence: Abstract and experiments (HTML full text): deterministic LIME (DLIME) vs LIME stability on 6 public and 6 synthetic tabular datasets
problem: LIME's random perturbation gives different explanations for the same prediction.
method: DLIME: agglomerative hierarchical clustering and KNN select a cluster; a linear model or tree trained on it gives deterministic explanations; stability measured as variability of selected feature sets (Jaccard) over repeated runs.
data: Three binary and three multi-class public datasets plus six synthetic datasets.
evaluation: Jaccard-based stability over repeated explanations; faithfulness.
findings: DLIME was deterministic and more stable than LIME while remaining faithful (abstract).
limitations: Ours: stability defined only as run-to-run feature-set variability; no input perturbation.
